newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-GASCOIGNE SCORES BUT RANGERS STUMBLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GASCOIGNE SCORES BUT RANGERS STUMBLE.

text.p: Rangers' Paul Gascoigne, who called himself "a disgrace" for being sent off against Ajax on Wednesday, ended a traumatic week on a slightly better note with an outstanding goal against Aberdeen on Saturday.
But his goal was not enough to bring Rangers a much-needed Scottish League victory as they conceded an 89th minute equaliser to allow Aberdeen to escape with a 2-2 draw.

Gascoigne, who was sent off in a European Cup Champions' League match in Amsterdam on Wednesday and, it is alleged, beat up his wife Sheryl last weekend, put Rangers ahead after 28 minutes with a 25-metre free kick that he shot high over the wall into the top right hand corner of the net.

Manager Walter Smith admitted he took a gamble on Gascoigne's mental state before picking him, but his risk seemed to have paid off as Rangers increased their lead when Danish international striker Brian Laudrup added a second after 37 minutes.
But Aberdeen fought back with a 40th minute goal from Brian Irvine and an 89th minute equaliser from Billy Dodds, the league's top scorer, who notched his 17th goal of the season.
The result means that Celtic, who trail Rangers by three points, will go top on goal difference if they beat Hearts on Sunday.

Hibernian, who last week became the first team to beat Rangers in the league this season, drew 1-1 at Motherwell, despite having goalkeeper Jim Leighton sent off after only 26 minutes for handling outside his area.
In the bottom-of-the-table clash, Kilmarnock beat Raith 2-1 to leave Raith firmly rooted to the foot of the standings.
